issue.title: reportRepo.create fails with "date/time field value out of range"
issue.body:
Our script creates one report per client per month through
`POST /api/v1/reports`. A bug on our side made it ask for February 2027 with
`"to": "2027-02-29"`, and the API answered `500 internal error`. The log line:

    {"level":"error","msg":"unhandled error","err":{"type":"DatabaseError","code":"22008","message":"date/time field value out of range: \"2027-02-29\"","stack":"error: date/time field value out of range: \"2027-02-29\"\n    at /srv/ledgerline/node_modules/pg/lib/client.js:535:17\n    at async Object.query (/srv/ledgerline/src/db/client.ts:27:22)\n    at async Object.one (/srv/ledgerline/src/db/client.ts:39:18)\n    at async Object.create (/srv/ledgerline/src/db/repos/reportRepo.ts:81:17)"}}

So the INSERT in `src/db/repos/reportRepo.ts` passes the dates in as plain
strings and Postgres chokes on them; `"to": "2026-04-31"` does the same. The
date was our mistake, but it should get a 400 that names the field, not a 500.

input.title: Reject calendar-invalid report dates with 400 instead of 500
input.body:
File: src/api/reports.ts

The isoDate schema (used for from and to in createSchema, reportFields and updateSchema) only checks the YYYY-MM-DD shape with a regex, so impossible dates such as 2027-02-29 or 2026-04-31 pass validation and fail in Postgres with code 22008, surfacing as a 500.

Proposed change: make isoDate also confirm the date exists on the calendar, for example by parsing it as UTC and checking that the year, month and day round-trip unchanged, and adding a refine with a message like "not a real calendar date". Zod then returns a 400 that names the field, as it already does for malformed dates. No change is needed in reportRepo.ts.

This comment was written by RepoMind, an automated triage agent. To reach a person, mention @ledgerline/maintainers.

The isoDate schema in this file only checks the YYYY-MM-DD shape, so calendar-impossible dates like 2027-02-29 and 2026-04-31 pass validation and reach Postgres, which rejects them as a 500. Running the suite, `test/reports.test.ts` passes in full, so no existing test covers an impossible date. I've opened draft PR pr-29 proposing that the schema also reject dates that don't exist, so the API returns a 400 naming the field. The repository layer is fine as it is.
